title: Non-uniform grids to accelerate electron-phonon coupling calculations for superconductivity
authors: Kang Wang, Siyu Chen, Sun-Woo Kim, Kieran Bozier, Chris Pickard, Bartomeu Monserrat
abstract: Efficient and accurate evaluation of electron-phonon interactions is essential for predictive superconductivity calculations, but dense Brillouin zone sampling requirements pose a major computational bottleneck. To overcome this, we introduce an accelerated, highly scalable framework that combines a double delta truncation scheme with non-uniform Farey grids in both $\mathbf{k}$ and $\mathbf{q}$ space. The truncation strategy significantly reduces computational cost by restricting integration to states satisfying energy constraints near the Fermi level, while the Farey grids dynamically resolve sampling errors from localized scattering and stabilize convergence. Applied to elemental aluminium and several high-pressure hydrides, this combined methodology reduces computational cost by up to two orders of magnitude and yields electron-phonon coupling constants and superconducting critical temperatures Tc typically within about 5% of full-grid benchmarks. This approach overcomes sampling bottlenecks associated with dense uniform grids, making accurate, low-cost predictions of superconductivity in complex quantum materials feasible.
summary: This paper presents a novel, highly efficient computational framework to calculate electron-phonon coupling for superconductivity. It combines double delta truncation with non-uniform Farey grids to drastically reduce the computational cost associated with dense Brillouin zone sampling. This breakthrough makes accurate, large-scale predictions of superconductivity in complex quantum materials feasible.
main_problem: Evaluating electron-phonon interactions for superconductivity is computationally bottlenecked by the dense Brillouin zone sampling required for accurate calculations.
main_result: The combined methodology reduces computational cost by up to two orders of magnitude while maintaining high accuracy, yielding $T_c$ predictions within 5% of full-grid benchmarks.
method: The authors combine a double delta truncation scheme to restrict integration near the Fermi level with non-uniform Farey grids to dynamically resolve sampling errors in both $\mathbf{k}$ and $\mathbf{q}$ space.
model_or_system: The study applies to calculating superconducting properties in various quantum materials, including elemental aluminum and several high-pressure hydrides ($	ext{CaH}_6$, $	ext{LaH}_{10}$).
key_observables: Electron-phonon coupling constant ($\lambda$), Eliashberg spectral function ($\alpha^2F(\omega)$), and superconducting critical temperature ($T_c$).
important_parameters: Fermi window width ($W$), Brillouin zone sampling density, and momentum transfer ($\mathbf{q}$).
main_assumptions: The method relies on the adiabatic approximation and assumes that the double delta truncation introduces a manageable, tunable underestimation of $\lambda$ that improves with increasing $W$.
figures_summary: Figures compare $\lambda$ and $\alpha^2F$ calculated using the new method versus full uniform grids, demonstrating excellent agreement alongside dramatic reductions in computational time.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the computational bottleneck, details the double delta truncation and Farey grid approach, applies it to various materials (Al, hydrides), and concludes by summarizing the efficient workflow combining both techniques.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state physics, the core contribution is a highly scalable and accurate numerical technique for integrating complex many-body integrals over momentum space, which has analogues in other quantum simulation domains.
